Groundwater forecasting · Bengaluru

Know how deep a well's water will be, weeks before it gets there.

Many homes and businesses in Bengaluru depend on borewells. Their water level rises with the monsoon, falls with pumping, and a well can run low with little warning. We built a proof of concept that turns routine pump records into forecasts for each well, with an honest range around every forecast.

See the models and the data ↓ Try a forecast for a well

The models and the data, at a glance

Two forecasting models are current. Each one is tested on its own simulated copy of the wells, because no real water-level measurement has been released yet.

Current model

ML forecaster

Reads how each well behaves from its own pump records, then a learning layer corrects the forecast. It looks from one day to twelve weeks ahead.

Data usedA five-year simulated copy of the 579 wells, calibrated to published Bengaluru observations: six kinds of well, paved city wards and real Bengaluru rainfall.

Result. Twelve weeks ahead the typical forecast is 0.70 m off, against 1.30 m for assuming nothing changes. One day ahead it is 0.18 m off.

See the ML forecaster →
Current model

Stage 2 · Physics + sensors

Separates the true water level from what the sensor reports, finds faulty sensors, and forecasts up to twelve weeks ahead.

Data usedOur own five-year simulated city of 579 wells, built twice in different ways, plus harder versions with well loss and a rain response calibrated to measured Bengaluru levels.

Result. Twelve weeks ahead the average forecast is 0.74 m off, against 1.48 m for trusting the latest reading. It finds 88 % of faulty sensors.

See Stage 2 →

The two models are tested on different simulated cities and measured in slightly different ways, so their numbers should not be compared with each other.

How we got here

Each step answered one question and set up the next.

STEP 1

Can pump records become forecasts?

Yes: a 15-day vendor export was cleaned, linked and modelled.

 STEP 2

What matters most: data or model?

Data. Resting-level readings cut error from 4.2 m to 0.5 m on a test system.

 STEP 3

How far ahead can we see?

Twelve weeks, at half the error of guessing, with honest ranges.

 STEP 4

Do wells affect each other?

In simulation, yes (a separate exploration). We know what data would measure it.

These four steps were iteration 1 (July–September 2026). The two current models, the ML forecaster and Stage 2 · Physics + sensors, came after.

Honest status

This is a proof of concept. Every result comes from simulated wells, and the 15-day vendor export carries demonstration water levels, so no real level measurement has been used yet. The next step is to repeat these tests on real long-term data. Here is what that needs.

Borewell Forecast is a proof of concept for forecasting groundwater levels in Bengaluru borewells. Results are labelled by where the data came from: vendor export (15 days, July 2026, in the vendor's real format but with demonstration water-level values), synthetic test system (450 simulated wells with a known answer) or digital twin (physics-based simulations of the 579 wells: one year in iteration 1, five years in later iterations and in Stage 2). No real water-level measurement has been used yet, and nothing here is yet a validated field forecast. Built by the FARII consortium.
